command: cat documents/opposing-counsel-cover-email.eml; parse-doc documents/mediated-settlement-agreement.docx | wc -c; parse-doc documents/proposed-final-decree.docx | wc -c

parse-doc docx documents/mediated-settlement-agreement.docx > /workspace/msa.txt; parse-doc docx documents/proposed-final-decree.docx > /workspace/dec.txt; wc -c /workspace/*.txt; cat /workspace/msa.txt

cd /tmp && for f in mediated-settlement-agreement proposed-final-decree; do mkdir -p $f && cd $f && unzip -o -q /workspace/documents/$f.docx && ls word; grep -c -E "w:vanish|w:del |w:ins |w:comment" word/document.xml; cd ..; done; python3 -c "import docx;print(docx.__version__ if hasattr(docx,\"__version__\") else 1)"; ls /workspace/skills/docx/scripts

mkdir -p /workspace/work && cat > /workspace/work/data.py <<"PYEOF"
# Each row: id, topic, msa, decree, analysis, severity, favors, recommendation
CATS = []

CATS.append(("A", "Structural, Incorporation and Execution Issues", [
("A-1", "No reference to or incorporation of the MSA",
 "MSA § 10.2: Decree “shall specifically reference this Mediated Settlement Agreement and shall be in all respects consistent with” it; in a conflict the MSA controls. See also MSA §§ 2, 11 (binding under Tex. Fam. Code §§ 6.602 and 153.0071(d)).",
 "Decree Arts. I–II contain no mention of the January 18, 2025 MSA. Art. I recites that “all matters in controversy were submitted to the Court for determination” and Art. II finds a “just and right division” under § 7.001, as though after a contested trial.",
 "Omitting the MSA removes the express conflict rule (MSA controls) and the textual anchor for enforcing the MSA’s terms; framing the decree as a contested adjudication rather than an agreed judgment on a § 6.602 / § 153.0071 MSA invites argument that the decree, not the MSA, defines the parties’ rights.",
 "High", "Derek",
 "Insert findings that the parties executed a binding, irrevocable MSA on January 18, 2025 complying with §§ 6.602(b) and 153.0071(d); that the Court approves it and renders judgment on it; that the MSA is incorporated by reference; and that any conflict is resolved in favor of the MSA. Re-caption as an Agreed Final Decree of Divorce."),
("A-2", "Client signature on a nonconforming decree may operate as an amendment of the MSA",
 "MSA § 10.5: the MSA may be modified only “by a written instrument signed by both parties.”",
 "Decree Art. XVII contains “APPROVED AND CONSENTED TO” signature lines for Megan and Derek; Steed’s March 7, 2025 email asks that Ms. Holloway sign and return the decree before the April 3 prove-up.",
 "A consent decree signed by both parties is itself a writing signed by both parties. If Ms. Holloway signs this draft, Respondent can argue that each deviation below was knowingly agreed and that the MSA was amended under § 10.5, waiving her right to judgment on the MSA terms.",
 "Critical", "Derek",
 "Ms. Holloway must not sign the draft. Counsel signature should be “Approved as to form only” until a fully conforming decree is agreed. Respond in writing that the draft does not conform and that Petitioner stands on the MSA."),
("A-3", "Opposing counsel’s representation of conformity",
 "N/A",
 "Cover email (Mar. 7, 2025): decree “was prepared consistent with the terms of the parties’ Mediated Settlement Agreement.”",
 "The representation is inaccurate. At least 60 substantive and clerical discrepancies were identified, and the financial ones run almost uniformly in Respondent’s favor (approximately $30,000 in property alone, plus a reversed medical-expense split, a lower child support figure, and a modifiable maintenance award). Several changes preserve the original totals (e.g., 401(k) and brokerage splits still sum to the account balance), which makes them easy to overlook.",
 "High", "Derek",
 "Correct the record in a written objection letter itemizing each discrepancy; preserve the email. Consider whether to request that Respondent’s counsel redline any future draft against the MSA."),
]))
